I have 13.1 mu total, so I will not spread myself too thin. I will keep the land arrangement close to what has been steady for me: about 8 mu in the wheat-maize rotation, and 5.1 mu in cotton. At my age, and with some family members working off-farm, I care more about a stable harvest than chasing the absolute highest yield. I have well irrigation, so I can protect wheat at the key stages, but pumping costs money, so I will not irrigate unless the crop stage and soil moisture justify it.

For wheat, I will stay with the local October sowing window and use an improved winter wheat seed that performs reliably here. I usually do better when I put most of the fertilizer down as base and then give one topdress at jointing, so I will keep that pattern. After wheat harvest, maize has to go in immediately. That turnaround is always tight, so I will use simple tillage or direct planting after a quick residue cleanup instead of doing heavy land preparation. On the cotton land, I will keep inputs moderate. Cotton can pay if the stand is good, but it ties up labor later in the season, so I will not push fertilizer too hard. I will watch insects closely because if aphids or bollworm get ahead of me, cotton gets expensive fast. Overall, my thinking is simple: protect wheat yield, get maize in on time, and keep cotton as a cash crop without overspending.
